key_insight: The paper combines Pauli propagation with noise-canceling inverse channels so observables are classically transformed into forms that can be measured with less sampling overhead on quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: This hybrid approach reduces both quantum measurement cost and classical truncation burden, making observable estimation more practical for near-term noisy quantum processors.
method: Propagate target observables through inverse noise channels on the classical side.
Measure the modified observable directly on the quantum processor.
Use truncation strategies to balance memory, runtime, and mitigation accuracy.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmarked the approach numerically on canonical challenging models and experimentally on a 56-qubit superconducting processor, comparing truncation tradeoffs.
watch_item: Performance depends on truncation strategy, so gains in sampling reduction can be offset if classical propagation is truncated too aggressively.
paper_title: Computing noise-canceling observables via Pauli propagation
